validator: draft 1 passed with no hard problems, no soft problems and no warnings. The faults below are the critic's.
keep: The idea is named in one plain sentence up front: one box per position, and only the box against the ports joins them.
Thirteen screens, SHOW 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 alternating with DO 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, ending with two mixed puzzles (12, 13). No recall opener, as the brief gives lesson 5 none.

Each lesson 5 slip in the brief has a DO screen with its own hint: ports and positions swapped (2 and 13, typed, with the swap as a slip), the box read in the wrong place (4, and 12 on a new valve), detent and spring confused (6), and a closed centre trusted to hold for ever (10, after the creep on 9).
The two counts (2, 13) are typed whole numbers; their wrong figures are slips with hints. The rest choose a port, a box or what the plant does, so they stay as options.

The cause is drawn: the ports stay fixed and the row slides under them, so he sees the box against the ports doing the work. The centre picker gives settings where the rod holds, and Float, where the same rest position lets the load move.
Safety comes first in practice: a centred valve is not proof a load is safe.
The analogy is from his trade, the intermediate switch, new to this course, with where it breaks.
Only the three sources that carry this idea are cited, each on words its quote supports. How valves are built and set is left out and said to be left out.
fix: Causal step skipped: explain says only the box against the ports joins them but never why. Add that the moving part is a spool, a rod with grooves, and sliding it lines different grooves up with the fixed ports; that is what each box stands for. This also defines 'spool' before paragraph 4 uses it.
Rule missing from explain: practice's rule of thumb, an actuator brings in the box beside it, is used on screens 3, 4 and 12 but explain only shows it for -Y1. State it as a general rule.

Contradiction in the picture: whatAmILookingAt says the held rod always creeps, then adds a Creep switch, and screen 9 says 'switch Creep on'. Make it one control, a Leaks switch, Off (the ideal the symbol stands for, the rod holds) and On (a real spool, the rod creeps from a mark), opening Off.
One verb for one event: the rod 'rises', 'comes out' and 'goes down'. Use 'comes out' and 'goes back in' throughout.

False absolutes: the analogy's 'exactly those two positions' and float's 'move the rod freely' (oil still has to flow out). Soften to 'those two positions' and 'push the rod along'. Screen 10's 'a part that seals' becomes 'a valve that seats tightly, such as a check valve'.

Footnotes carry reasoning their quotes lack: [^2] is on 'with nothing operating it', [^3] on 'oil' where the quote is about air. Split [^2] so it sits on 'normal or neutral position', and word [^3]'s sentence for pressure in general. Name T as the return to the tank, as [^1]'s quote says Return.
Screen 6 is close to recall: its choices say 'springs' and 'detent', the words the SHOW screen just used. Make the choices the marks he must read: zigzags at its ends, a notched bar.
The pump at the end of the stroke is not described: with -Y1 held and the rod fully out, the oil goes over the relief valve. Say so, so the pump line never shows 'feeding' with nowhere to feed.
Ignores carries a strange line ('the cylinder only moves its own load'): replace with what the model really leaves out, friction and a load that never changes.
Screen 12 never says where the 3/2's spring is: add a spring at the right end, so the slide back has a cause.
